note: Re-judged on 2026-09-20 by an independent reader, after Negotiate's signature moved from (local, remote []Capability, localASN, peerASN uint32) to (local, remote []Capability, identity PeerIdentity). Inside each unit named here the change is one line, the call shape, and every assertion is byte-identical (git diff HEAD over internal/core/bgp/capability/negotiated_test.go). The new shape cannot move what these cases prove: Negotiate reads identity only where it stores LocalASN and PeerASN on the Negotiated, and where buildSubComponents copies the struct into n.Identity. No branch in Negotiate, and none in negotiatePathsLimitDirection, reads Internal or either AS number, so the iBGP verdict the struct now carries has no path to the PATHS-LIMIT maps. The identity each call passes is self-consistent too: 65001 against 65002 with Internal left false is an external session, which is what the two positional AS numbers meant before. Section 3: "An AFI/SAFI tuple MUST be ignored if the same tuple was not received in the ADD-PATH capability." TestNegotiatePathsLimitPartialAddPath carries both polarities on two distinct assertions, not one assertion wearing two hats: ipv4/unicast is present in ADD-PATH, so its tuple applies in both directions and is pinned at 10 and 5, and ipv6/unicast is absent from ADD-PATH while its PATHS-LIMIT tuple sits in the same capability, so both directions must stay zero. The buffer isolates this rule: both sides advertise Multiprotocol for ipv6/unicast, so ipv6 is a negotiated family and the only thing that can drop its tuple is the ADD-PATH check. Were ipv6 missing from Multiprotocol, the family intersection would decide the case and the test would prove nothing here. Same producing branch as 3-2, evaluated per family; remove it and ipv6 reads 8 and 3. No discrimination record: the tags predate HEAD. 2026-09-26 RE-AUDIT, stale-requirement: the checklist line lost its quotation marks and gained the sentence's full stop, so it is now a verbatim span of Section 3 of rfc/drafts/draft-abraitis-idr-addpath-paths-limit.txt. The obligation is the sentence this note already quotes, and the tagged units are byte-identical (TestNegotiatePathsLimitNoAddPath re-read this pass: both PATHS-LIMIT maps must stay zero with no ADD-PATH). Verdict unchanged.
